subject: Velociti renewal — flexible cushion proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Velociti renewal — flexible cushion proposal

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our notes, I wanted to put a concrete renewal/expansion path on paper so your procurement team has something to review. High-level proposal:

- Term: 12 months (start: 2027-04-01)
- Baseline commit: 20% uplift on current committed units (applies to compute/throughput units)
- Flex cushion: an on-demand mid-contract top-up facility (monthly top-ups), billed pro-rata, with smoothing credits if annualized at next renewal
- Pricing: laddered uplift discounts (see attached deck): 0–39% uplift = list uplift price; 40–99% uplift = 10% off uplift unit price; 100%+ = 15% off uplift price
- Co-term path: option to co-term with your existing vendor date (2027-03-31) via a pro-rata true-up and credit to smooth invoicing

I attached a short pricing deck and a term-sheet that shows the three suggested options (conservative, volume, committed-cushion). If helpful, we can prepare an amendment draft that legal/procurement can redline.

Are you available for a 30-min slot Tuesday or Wednesday to walk procurement through the mechanics? If procurement prefers to review first, we can give a 7–10 day window for feedback.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com]
Attachments: velociti_pricing_deck_v2.pdf, redwood_flex_cushion_term_sheet.xlsx
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@velocitihealth.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Velociti renewal — flexible cushion proposal

Jordan,

Appreciate the clear options. Procurement has a couple of asks before we can move to a verbal agreement:

1) We need the renewal to be able to co-term with an existing contract that lapses 2027-03-31. Can you show the pro-rata math and whether we can net invoices to a single co-term date?
2) Mid-contract top-ups: procurement wants assurance that monthly top-ups won’t carry a retroactive price step mid-billing cycle and that invoice smoothing will be available.
3) If we commit to >40% uplift, we need confirmation of the 10% uplift discount and a simple T&Cs callout (no hidden fees). Also need an expected ARR delta for budget planning.

They asked me to get a draft amendment and a sample SOW redline. If you can loop in legal/finance and send a draft by EOD Wednesday that would be ideal. I’ll coordinate with our procurement lead (procurement@velocitihealth.com) for the review timeline.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of AI Platforms | Velociti Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Velociti renewal — flexible cushion proposal

Alex — thanks, understood. Quoting your asks below for clarity:

> 1) co-term math and single invoicing to 2027-03-31
> 2) assurance on monthly top-ups and smoothing
> 3) confirmation of 10% discount >40% uplift and ARR delta

Proposed response and options (attached: velociti_pricing_deck_v2.pdf, velociti_amendment_draft.docx):

Option A — Minimal change (fastest):
- Keep 12-month renewal beginning 2027-04-01. Allow monthly top-ups billed pro-rata. No guaranteed price lock for top-ups beyond quarter.
- Co-term via pro-rata true-up at 2027-03-31; invoices remain separate but a credit memo will be issued to align charges on one monthly statement.
- Uplift discounts: standard list price on initial 20% uplift.

Option B — Volume tier (recommended by Finance):
- Add explicit tier: 40–99% uplift -> 10% off uplift unit price; 100%+ -> 15% off uplift unit price.
- Monthly top-ups billed monthly; if cumulative top-ups within the contract reach a higher tier, we apply an end-of-term true-up refund/credit on uplift units to reflect the tiered price (smoothing).
- Co-term handled via a single-invoice option: we combine charges into one statement and provide a one-time invoice credit to align period.

Option C — Committed cushion (preferred for predictable pricing):
- Increase baseline commit to lock rates for any mid-contract top-ups up to an agreed cushion % (e.g., +50% of baseline). Billing monthly; top-ups counted toward committed units immediately.
- Deeper discount (12–18%) for larger term and commit.

ARR impact: Ben and I ran a quick model — Option B at your expected 60% uplift yields an ARR increase of roughly $420k (±5%) versus current run-rate; we’ll attach the simple P&L table in the deck.

Next steps: I’ll let Ben upload the P&L table; Kimberly, can legal review the amendment draft for the co-term/credit mechanics and flag any redlines? If acceptable, I’ll prepare a DocuSign packet and PO instructions for Alex’s procurement team.

Regards,
Jordan

--

Subject: Re: Velociti renewal — flexible cushion proposal

Jordan — quick legal/ops note on the amendment draft you attached:

1) Co-term mechanics: we should avoid moving primary SLA windows unless Velociti explicitly requests it. The amendment will implement the pro-rata true-up and invoice credit approach; we will not change the SLA start/stop dates unless there is a signed addendum.
2) Top-up billing: we’ll include a clause that monthly top-ups are billed at the uplift unit price and that any retrospective tier adjustments will be handled via a one-time true-up credit at the next invoice cycle.
3) Pricing guarantees: legal recommends limiting long-term price locks to the committed-cushion option (Option C) and keeping volume tier discounts as commercial terms (not embedded into the master service agreement).

Attached is an internal redline (velociti_amendment_draft.docx) with bracketed language for procurement to review. If Ben can confirm the P&L figures are final, we’ll prepare a clean amendment for signature.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Jordan/Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement is comfortable proceeding with Option B (volume tier) subject to a 30-day final review window. A few confirmations before we sign:

- Please include the clause that monthly top-ups are billed monthly and that end-of-term true-up credits will be issued to retroactively apply the correct tiered price.
- Confirm that co-term will be reflected by a single invoice option and that Redwood will issue the pro-rata credit as described.
- Please send a DocuSign packet and PO instructions so procurement can route internally.

If you can get the DocuSign link and the PO flow by EOD tomorrow, we can start the 30-day review. Procurement contact is procurement@velocitihealth.com.

Alex
